tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use it when...'), focuses on user-facing trigger scenarios (model invocation errors, KB returning stale/nothing, etc.) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly pushes coverage even when the user doesn't name the domain terms ('Use it even if they don't name invocation logging, SCPs, marketplace subscriptions...'). It also explicitly carves out what it is NOT for, reducing false triggers. It is a dense but reasonably concise paragraph given the complexity of the scope boundary it must convey.
tests.evidence: Review Amazon Bedrock configuration, model access and Knowledge Bases (RAG), read-only. Use it when a Bedrock call fails with an access, validation or throttling error... Use it even if they don't name invocation logging, SCPs, marketplace subscriptions, chunking, embeddings, vector stores or hybrid search.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but nearly all content is project-specific: check-id families, routing tables, guardrails specific to this account-masking requirement, severity derivations. There's no explanation of generic concepts like what Bedrock or RAG is in general terms — it jumps straight into domain-specific conventions.
tests.evidence: Every finding is grounded in a catalog under `references/` with a stable check-id, a severity and an AWS-doc citation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (check catalogs, metric thresholds, API quirks, playbooks) is consistently pushed to references/ files, not embedded in the body. The body's tables are routing/severity summaries, not detailed lookup data.
tests.evidence: load before raising any LLM-INV finding (the LLM-INV-001..015 catalog).

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked with a markdown link in the body, in both the routing table and the References section.
tests.evidence: [model-access-review.md](references/model-access-review.md): load first for a model access or configuration question

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link in the References section and the routing table specifies the condition under which to load it (e.g., before raising a finding, while running a step, when interpreting a response).
tests.evidence: [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md): load before interpreting a response that looks wrong (§1–17 shared and model access, §18–19 knowledge base access and throttling).

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/compliance-critical operations (account ID masking, read-only guardrails, severity assignment) are stated as strict rules, while the area-selection and routing logic explain reasoning (why access-denied differs by API) giving flexibility in diagnosis, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: Never call a mutating API. Recommend the fix, state the exact CLI or IaC change and let the user run it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools/approaches as equal options for the same task; the routing table assigns one clear reference/template per scenario rather than offering a menu.
tests.evidence: No menu of equal alternative tools is presented; each row in the routing table maps to one specific reference and template.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable approach (pick area, read router file, apply check catalog, bound scope, report with severities) applicable to any Bedrock/RAG review request, not a one-off task declaration.
tests.evidence: Name the area, then read its review file **before the first API call**. Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure, the pre-presentation checks...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes concrete, non-obvious corrections (account ID leakage patterns, access-denied vs throttling area distinctions, chunk-text withholding) that function as gotchas even without a dedicated heading.
tests.evidence: Live runs leaked it in lines like "The account (`<12 digits>`) is in my enabled associations"... Each of those is a breach, even when the user pasted the ID first.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured posture reports and provides dedicated templates in assets/ for each area, satisfying the need for output templates.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output templates are embedded inline in the body; templates are kept in assets/ and only referenced, with just a short severity table inline.
tests.evidence: load only when the user asks for a full written report, one per area.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both asset files are linked in the body's routing table and References section.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset links specify exactly when to load them — only when a full written report is requested, and which template maps to which area via the table.
tests.evidence: load only when the user asks for a full written report, one per area.

tests.name: Asset path format

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The SKILL.md body itself does not lay out a monolithic ordered step-by-step procedure in the main file (procedures live in the referenced playbook files); the body instead focuses on routing, guardrails and definitions, so the checklist requirement doesn't apply to the body content shown here.
tests.evidence: Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure, the pre-presentation checks, the check family, common wrong answers and error handling for that area.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly instructs self-validation before presenting, requiring checks on evidence, check-ids, severity thresholds, and account-ID leakage before finishing the answer.
tests.evidence: Evidence or silence. Every finding cites the concrete value that triggered it. Distinguish "measured zero" from "no data reported" or "no job to read"
